question: Who among the following is known as the tabla maestro?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ustad Zakir Hussain**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zakir Hussain is an Indian tabla player,** composer, percussionist, music producer and film actor.
 
• **Popularly known as the Tabla Maestro**, Ustad Zakir Hussain is arguably the most famous Tabla player in our country in the post-independence era. 
 
• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1988, and the Padma Bhushan in 2002, by the Government of India presented by President Abdul Kalam.
 
• The pre-eminent tabla virtuoso of time, Zakir is one of the world's great musicians, esteemed as a groundbreaking collaborator, composer, and cultural icon.
 
• Born to tabla maestro, Alla Rakha and Bavi Begum in Mahim, Mumbai on March 9, 1951, Zakir Hussain had an inclination for playing the tabla at a very young age.
 
• Hussain learned to play the mridang (a classical percussion instrument) from his father when he was just 3 and began performing at concerts by the age of 12.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ustad Bismillah Khan ****​**

 
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan used to play Shehnai.
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916 – 2006) (Real name is Qamaruddin Khan), was an Indian musician credited with popularizing the Shehnai.
 
• Shehnai is a musical instrument that is similar to the oboe (common in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.)
 
• He was felicitated with several awards including:
 
 
• Padma Shri in 1961
 
• Padma Bhushan in 1968
 
• Padma Vibhushan in 1980
 
• Bharat Ratna in 2001
 
 
 
• He also played the Shehnai at the 1st Republic Day celebration in 1950.
 
 
 
• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan
 
 
• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan born on 9th October 1945 is an Indian classical sarod player, best known for his clear and fast ekhara taans.
 
• Ustad Amjad Khan was honored with Padma Shri in 1975, Padma Bhushan in 1991, and Padma Vibhushan in 2001.
 
• Ustad Amjad Khan was also awarded 21st Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavna Award, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1989, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 2011.
 
• Sarod: It is a stringed instrument.
 
• Sarod known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound, widely used in folk music.
 
• The U.S. state of Massachusetts proclaimed 20 April as Amjad Ali Khan Day in 1984.
 
 
 
• **Ghulam Ali****​**
 
 
• Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was born in Kasur, of the erstwhile Punjab Province, British India in 1902
 
• Following the partition of India in 1947, Kasur Tehsil was allocated to Pakistan. At the age of five, Bade Ghulam began training in vocal music from his chacha Kale Khan, and later from his father.
 
• The most famous stalwart of Hindustani music, Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was frustrated with a social set-up that found it difficult to honour his gift as a singer and migrated to India in the early '50s.
